tagline: Post GitHub PR and issue notifications to Discord developer communities
metaTitle: GitHub Discord Integration: PR, CI and Release Alerts
metaDescription: Post PR merges, CI status and new releases with changelogs to Discord and flag good first issues for contributors. GAIA formats each alert. See the setup steps.
intro:
Source-available projects and developer communities live on Discord, but activity in the repository stays siloed unless someone manually posts updates. Contributors miss important issues and PRs because they are not watching the repository. Maintainers spend time copying links into announcements by hand. Community members who want to contribute have no easy way to find what needs help without digging through GitHub's interface.

GAIA connects the two to keep your developer community informed and engaged automatically. When a new issue is opened, a PR is merged, or a release is published, GAIA formats the event into a clean message and routes it to the right channel. Members can react, discuss, and open the original item on GitHub without maintainers doing any manual announcement work.

The integration is essential for source-available project maintainers who want active contributor communities, for developer-focused companies running public servers, and for internal engineering teams that use Discord as their primary communication platform and want real-time code activity feeds.

useCases.title: Post PR merge announcements to a channel
useCases.description: When a pull request merges to the main branch, GAIA sends a formatted announcement to your #releases or #dev-activity channel, including the PR title, author, a summary of changes, and a link to the full diff.

useCases.title: Alert contributors to issues tagged 'good first issue'
useCases.description: GAIA monitors the repository for newly opened issues labeled 'good first issue' or 'help wanted' and posts them to a dedicated channel so community contributors can immediately see where they can jump in and help.

useCases.title: Real-time CI/CD status in Discord
useCases.description: GAIA posts CI workflow results to the channel so the team knows immediately when a build passes or fails. Failed builds include a direct link to the failing step so engineers can triage without switching back to the repo.

useCases.title: New release notifications with changelog
useCases.description: When a new release is published, GAIA formats the release notes and posts them to the channel with a download link, version number, and any breaking changes highlighted so community members are always informed about new versions.

useCases.title: Daily digest for contributors
useCases.description: Each day GAIA posts a digest of the previous day's repository activity to the channel: merged PRs, resolved issues, new contributors, and open PRs awaiting review, keeping the entire community informed at a glance.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Discord to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your repository or organization and your server in GAIA's settings. GAIA uses a bot with webhook access so you control exactly which channels receive which notifications.

Configure which events (issues, PRs, releases, CI runs) should post to which channels. You can filter by repository, branch, label, or event type so each channel receives only relevant, focused updates.

howItWorks.step: GAIA delivers activity to your channels automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA processes GitHub webhook events and formats them into rich messages with relevant context, links, and formatting. Your community stays informed without any manual announcement effort from maintainers.

faqs.question: Can I customize the format of notifications posted to channels?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA supports customizable message templates for each event type. You can control which fields are included, adjust the embed colors, add custom text, and configure whether messages appear as simple text or rich embeds with thumbnails and action buttons.

faqs.question: Can GAIA handle multiple repositories in one server?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. You can connect multiple repositories to a single server and route each repository's events to different channels. For example, a mono-repo organization might route frontend PRs to #frontend-dev and backend PRs to #backend-dev.

faqs.question: Is this only for public source-available projects?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA works equally well for private repositories and internal engineering teams that use a chat platform for communication. All repository data is handled securely, and GAIA only posts to the channels you configure with the permissions you grant.
